review.body: The kurta itself is lovely, nothing wrong with the fabric or stitching. Problem is I ordered L and got M, and the exchange took more than three weeks with two follow-ups to customer care. Wanted it for a wedding and ended up wearing something else.
review.title: Nice kurta, painful exchange

review.body: Installation guy came 6 days late and left the inlet pipe leaking. Called customer care three times, no proper response. Cant comment on the water taste yet because I'm still waiting for someone to fix it.
review.title: Installation was a nightmare

review.body: I'm training for my first half marathon and have put roughly 250 km on these over two months, mostly early morning road runs of 8-14 km. The cushioning under the heel hasn't gone flat yet, which was my main worry at this price. Upper mesh is breathable enough for Pune humidity and my socks don't come out soaked. No hot spots or blisters even on the long Sunday run. The outsole is showing a little wear at the outer heel but that's just how I land. Would buy again when these retire.
review.title: Clocked 250 km, still bouncy

review.body: For a hardcover with colour photos on every page, 549 is value for money. Made the coconut chutney and the vegetable stew this week, both came out well.
Conection drops constantly. Recieved it yesterday.

Seeing the other reviews I was nervous, but my installation was done the next day and the technician was polite and tidy. Water tastes good and the UV indicator is handy. If your area has good service coverage, go for it.
review.title: Smooth setup in my case

review.body: Superb ANC at this price. Very happy.

Honestly the buying experience was poor. The installation was scheduled for the day after delivery but the technician came a full week later, was in a hurry, and drilled the holes slightly crooked. I had to call customer care twice just to get the free pre-filter they had promised. Having said all that, now that it is running the water tastes clean and slightly sweet, and my TDS meter reads around 80 compared to 600 from the borewell. So the product is good, the service around it is not.
review.title: Bad installation experience, good water

review.body: The purifier itself works but the after-sales model is designed to squeeze you. Every service visit outside the AMC is charged ₹450 even if the technician just looks at it for five minutes. They keep calling to push a ₹3,500 yearly AMC and when I said no, the next filter change somehow took three weeks to schedule. Membrane replacement was quoted at ₹2,200 at the one-year mark. Factor all of this into the price because the sticker price is only half the story with AquaFresh.
review.title: Service costs add up

review.body: Quiet, beautiful book. Cried at the end.
बहुत अच्छा तेल है, दो हफ्ते में बाल झड़ना कम हो गया। खुशबू थोड़ी तेज़ है।
Same three ideas repeated for 90 days. I cant understand how this got such good ratings, maybe it works if you have never read anything on mindfulness before.
review.title: Very repetative

review.body: Super comfy, did 10k on day one itself. No blisters.

Using it every day for my office commute by local train. The padded laptop sleeve fits my 15.6 inch laptop with a little room to spare, and there's still space for a lunch box, charger and a rain jacket in the main compartment. The canvas held up well in a proper Mumbai downpour, everything inside stayed dry, though the outside took a while to dry. Shoulder straps are padded enough that it doesn't dig in even when the bag is full. Zips run smoothly and feel sturdy.
review.title: My daily commute bag now

review.body: light weight, good grip on treadmill. worth for money
Superb thriller, go for it!
Solid laptop for the money. No complaints so far.
Fast paced and the descriptions of Hampi at night are really vivid. The ending felt rushed though, the detective explains everything in one long speech and a few coincidences were hard to buy.
review.title: Gripping until the last 30 pages

review.body: Filled it with ice and water at 7 am before a road trip, left it in a parked car in Chennai heat for most of the afternoon, and there was still ice rattling inside at 3 am the next morning when we reached. The lid seal is leak-proof, I keep it sideways in my backpack with my laptop and not a drop has come out. The powder coat hasn't scratched much either. Superb bottle, my husband has already taken it over.
review.title: Ice for 20 hours, no kidding

review.body: Trims beard. Does what it says.
Several code samples use library versions that are two or three years old, and a couple didn't even run for me without changes. Still, the principles behind them hold up, so it was worth reading.
review.title: Good ideas, dated examples

review.body: The silicone strap gave me a rash on the wrist within a week, had to buy a nylon one separately. The app also logs me out every few days. Still, for 4.5k with SpO2 and calling, it's worth it.
review.title: Strap is the weak link

review.body: There was a strong plastic smell for the first three or four runs even after doing an empty cycle like the manual says. It's gone now and the food comes out really well, but it was worrying for a while.
review.title: Smell on first few uses

review.body: Bought this after comparing with mats twice the price. Cushioning is good, the anti-slip texture works on my tiled floor and it rolls up tight with the strap. Value for money, honestly.
review.title: Value for money mat

review.body: Light, heats up fast, fine for daily shirts.
Good resistance range and the handles are comfy.

I've been a backend developer for about four years and Code Habits is the first book in a while that actually changed what I do day to day. The chapter on naming alone is worth it, and the section on writing tests before refactoring legacy modules was exactly what our team needed. Examples are in Python and JavaScript, short enough to follow without a laptop open. It doesn't preach, it just shows a messy function and then improves it step by step. I keep a copy on my desk now.
review.title: Changed how I review PRs

review.body: Liked it a lot in the first couple of weeks. Then the front pocket zip started catching on the fabric every single time, and now I have to hold the edge flat to close it. The side bottle pocket is too shallow, my 1 litre bottle fell out twice while I was climbing stairs. I also noticed the stitching where the left strap joins the bag has started fraying a little. For something I bought specifically for daily college use, I expected it to last longer than a month without issues.
review.title: Zip started catching in a month

review.body: Fabric is okay, fitting is regular. Nothing special but fine for office wear. Colour hasn't faded after 5-6 washes.
review.title: Decent office shirt

review.body: Wow, a speaker that disconnects every ten minutes. Exactly what I wanted for a house party.
review.title: Fantastic.

review.body: Ordered this for my father's 60th birthday. He's particular about fit around the chest and usually complains that ready-made kurtas are too tight there, so I measured one of his old kurtas and compared it with the size chart. Went with XL and it fit him perfectly, sleeves and length both spot on. It came neatly folded in a cloth bag instead of a plastic cover, which felt like a nice touch for a gift. He has worn it three times in two weeks already, which says enough.
review.title: Bought for my father's birthday

review.body: The sound quality is honestly great for the price, bass is punchy without getting muddy. Battery backup is the weak point though, with ANC on I'm charging it every second day.
review.title: Great sound, battery not so much

review.body: My physiotherapist recommended bands for knee rehab and these work fine for that. If you are already lifting weights, even the heaviest black band will feel light.
Elegant dial, keeps perfect time. Dad loved it.
Upgraded from a four year old phone and everything just feels faster. Fingerprint sensor is quick, face unlock works even in low light. Feels solid in hand, not plasticky at all.
Gifted it to my mom, she loves it 😊

I don't know how people use this overnight. I applied it before bed once, like the bottle suggests, and the onion smell soaked right into my pillow cover. Washed the cover twice and it's still faintly there. My husband refused to sleep on that side lol. The oil itself is thin and spreads easily, I'll give it that, but I'm not using something I can still smell on myself the next afternoon at office. Never again.
review.title: My pillow smells of onions

review.body: Hardware is honestly decent. The screen is bright, the watch faces look nice, and it survived a full monsoon season of me forgetting to take it off in the rain. What lets it down is the PulseFit app. Syncing fails about half the time and I have to toggle Bluetooth on my phone to get it to connect again. Workout history sometimes vanishes after a sync. If they fix the app with updates this could be a 4 star watch, right now it's average.
review.title: Mixed feelings after two months

review.body: Really solid pair. The app lets you tweak the EQ and I turned down the bass a little, now it sounds much more balanced. Folding hinge feels sturdy. Would have given 5 if the case was smaller.

The handle rod is longer than I'd like, so the inner plates knock my thighs during curls. Paint chipped off two plates in the first month and the threads need wiping or the collar gets stiff. Still, for home workouts at this price it's worth buying.
review.title: Few annoyances but still worth it

review.body: Didn't expect much at under 8k but the build feels premium, matte finish doesn't show fingerprints and the cushions are memory foam. Pairing with my laptop and phone at the same time works without fuss.
review.title: Pleasantly surprised

review.body: The plastic guard comb cracked at the clip after about five weeks of normal use, and the trimmer is useless for longer lengths without it. Customer care asked me to send photos and then stopped replying.
review.title: Guard comb snapped

review.body: Im a complete beginner and started yoga at home during the summer holidays with my daughter. We share this mat and it has held up really well, no tearing at the corners even though we roll and unroll it alot. It is thick enough for surya namaskar on a marble floor. Only reason for 4 stars is that the edges curled slightly in the first week, I had to roll it the opposite way overnight to fix it. For a home user like me this is more than enough.
review.title: Beginner's review after 3 months

review.body: Plates fit tight, no rattle. Very happy.
Cap was not sealed properly and half the oil had leaked by the time it reached me. Everything else in the box was greasy and stank. Haven't even used it, cant say anything about the oil itself.
review.title: Bottle leaked all over the parcel

review.body: It works the way it's supposed to. I just don't end up using it as often as I thought I would, mostly for reheating pizza. Probably more useful for bigger families who make snacks daily.

I picked this up after a friend kept going on about it and I'm glad I did. The story follows three generations of a trading family in coastal Karnataka, and the ledger itself becomes this quiet thread connecting everyone's secrets. The prose is unhurried but never boring, and the monsoon chapters are so atmospheric I could almost smell wet earth. Some reviewers say the first fifty pages are slow, which is fair, but stick with it. Paper quality is good and the cover is lovely in person.
review.title: A family saga that earns its length

review.body: I commute by two-wheeler for almost an hour every day, so sunscreen is non-negotiable for me. Most SPF 50 creams I've tried either leave my face looking ashy or turn into an oil slick by noon. Sunveil's matte one dries down in about a minute, sits fine under a helmet without sliding into my eyes, and doesn't sting. I reapply at lunch over a bit of compact powder and it doesn't pill. The tube is small for the price if you use the proper two-finger amount, that's the only thing.
review.title: The only sunscreen I actually reapply

review.body: Keeps chai hot till evening. Bit heavy when full.

This is my third tub. I have acne-prone skin and most moisturisers either feel like a layer of grease or clog my pores within days. This one is a clear gel, slightly cooling when you apply it, and it never feels heavy even when I travel somewhere humid like Mumbai. There's no added fragrance so nothing irritates. One tub lasts around two months with twice daily use. The flip cap is a bit flimsy, it cracked on my second tub, but the product itself is excellent and easily worth the price.
review.title: Repurchased three times now

review.body: Very light, maybe the lightest shoe I own, and the mesh keeps my feet cool even in May. Cushioning is soft without feeling mushy. My one real complaint is grip on wet surfaces. During the first monsoon runs I nearly slipped twice on painted road markings and the tiled entrance of my society, so now I'm careful on rainy days. On dry tarmac and the treadmill it's totally fine. If the rubber was grippier this would be a five star shoe for me.
Light, compact and perfect for my hostel room.

From day one it disconnected randomly, sometimes in the middle of a song, sometimes when the phone was right next to it. I tried two phones and a laptop, same result, so it's the speaker. Raised a warranty claim and was told to courier it to Bangalore at my own cost. Three weeks later they sent back the same unit with a note saying 'no fault found'. It still disconnects. Not buying anything from this brand again.
review.title: Disconnects, then the warranty runaround

review.body: Step count and sleep tracking match my old fitness band pretty closely. Battery backup is around 8 days with notifications on. Bluetooth calling is usable indoors, voice sounds a bit robotic to the other person.
review.title: Good fitness band for the price

review.body: Coming from an LCD phone, the display on this is a huge jump. Deep blacks, smooth scrolling, readable even in afternoon sun. Battery gets me through a full day with around 30% left.
review.title: That AMOLED screen

review.body: I write for a living and the keyboard is the main reason I picked this one. Keys are quiet with a nice soft bottom, no flex in the middle of the deck. The aluminium lid feels solid and there's barely any wobble when I open it with one hand. Trackpad is accurate though a bit small compared to what I had before. Haven't had a single crash or freeze since I got it in July.
review.title: Typing on it all day

review.body: This is my second Kaari kurta and the first one is still going strong after a year of regular wear. At this price for real handloom cotton, it's honestly value for money.

Tracking showed delivered on the 12th but I actually recieved it 9 days later, with the box torn open on one side. Messaged the seller twice and got no reply. Haven't used the bag yet so can't say anything about the bag itself, this rating is for the experience.
review.title: Late delivery, torn box, no reply

review.body: Boils a full litre in a few minutes and the auto cut-off has worked every single time. Handle stays cool. Wish the cord was a bit longer, but that's minor.

Cleans the air well and the auto mode reacts quickly when someone is cooking. But the replacement HEPA filter costs ₹2,800 and they suggest changing it every six months, which nobody mentions upfront.
review.title: Check the filter price before buying

review.body: Was happy for the first month. Then a system update came, and after installing it the phone started restarting by itself, sometimes four or five times a day. Touch also stops responding randomly. I did a factory reset as the Novaphone service centre suggested and lost my WhatsApp chats in the process, problem still there. They're now saying I have to wait for the next patch. A phone that reboots in the middle of a UPI payment is not usable, simple as that.
review.title: Update broke the phone

review.body: It's fine. Common sense advice, mostly.
Light gel that disappears into the skin in seconds. My T-zone stays less shiny till lunch and there's no fragrance at all, which I prefer. Sits well under sunscreen.

The fabric was cardboard-stiff out of the box, it took about four washes before it felt comfortable. Even now the sleeves end above my wrist bone and I'm only 5'11. Looks good though when the sleeves are rolled up.
review.title: Stiff at first, sleeves run short

review.body: Please be careful with this one. During my third set of overhead presses the locking collar on the left side spun loose and two plates slid off, missing my foot by inches. I checked afterwards and the thread on the rod is shallow, the collar only bites for about one and a half turns. I tightened it properly the next day and it loosened again after twenty reps. For something that goes over your head this is not acceptable. Requested a return.
review.title: Collar came loose mid-set

review.body: Battery lasts me the whole week of commuting.

I take the metro for almost an hour each way and these have changed that completely. The noise cancelling is strong enough that I can hear announcements only if I switch to ambient mode, which is one tap on the left cup. Sound is warm and detailed, vocals come through clearly and the bass doesn't overpower everything. I wore them for a full 9 hour flight last month and my ears didn't hurt, the cushions are soft and the headband clamp is just right. Battery lasted the flight and then some. I was sceptical about Auralis since I'd never heard of them but no regrets.
review.title: Best purchase this year for my commute

review.body: Beautiful colour and so soft. Got many compliments 😊
Pictures are stunning and the recipes mostly work. But two of the rasam recipes had way too much salt for us, and some places just say 'a handful' which isn't very helpful for beginners.
review.title: Gorgeous photos, check the salt

review.body: Picked this up in the Diwali sale for under 5k and it's been value for money. Controls are simple enough that my mother uses it on her own for reheating rotis and making makhana.
review.title: Value for money in the sale

review.body: Music sounds pleasant on the Buds Air, a little bass heavy but I like that. Touch controls take some getting used to, I kept pausing songs by accident while adjusting them. Calls are where they fall apart. Anywhere with wind or traffic the other person can barely hear me. Also the case hinge already feels loose after two months, it doesn't snap shut the way it did at first.
review.title: Good for music, bad for calls

review.body: Roomy, sturdy, zips feel strong. Good buy.
Average mixer. Nothing to complain, nothing to praise.

One clash with my partner's racket during a doubles rally and there's now a hairline crack at the throat. Strings had already snapped once before that. Graphite should handle a normal clash, not great.
review.title: Frame cracked in a month

review.body: Heats evenly and the weight is comfortable for long ironing sessions. But the non-stick soleplate started peeling near the tip after four months and now it sometimes drags on synthetic fabric.
review.title: Soleplate coating peeled

review.body: Good shirt for the price. Wear it to office weekly.
Does what a yoga mat should do.
The finish is lovely, no grease and makeup sits well on top. But if I sweat even a little and it gets near my eyes, they start watering. Now I just avoid applying close to the eye area.
review.title: Matte finish is great, eyes sting a bit

review.body: Compared it with the pulse oximeter at home and the heart rate was off by 15-20 bpm during walks. Whats the point of a fitness watch if the numbers are wrong.
review.title: Heart rate not acurate

review.body: I'm on the slimmer side and usually regular fits look like a tent on me. The slim fit here sits well at the shoulders and chest. Ironing takes a little effort but the collar holds its shape.
review.title: Neat fit for a slim build

review.body: During the hot months this was honestly all I needed, a pea-sized amount and my face felt hydrated without any shine. Now that the weather has turned dry in Delhi my cheeks feel tight by evening and there are flaky patches around my nose, so I've had to layer a heavier cream on top at night. Great if your skin is properly oily or for summer, but don't expect it to carry you through a North Indian winter.
review.title: Good in summer, not enough in winter

review.body: Water had a plastic taste for the whole first week. I boiled and threw it out maybe 8-10 times before it went away. Now it's fine and boils quickly, but the first impression was bad.
review.title: That plastic smell though

review.body: You can actually see and feel the weave, with tiny irregularities in the thread that tell you it's handloom and not a printed mill fabric. The cotton is soft and breathes really well, I wore it for a full day of Onam visits in humid weather and stayed comfortable. The colour is a deep indigo that looks richer in person than on the website. I hand washed it in cold water with mild detergent as the tag suggests and there was barely any colour in the water. Length is good for wearing with jeans or churidar.
review.title: Proper handloom, not a print

review.body: Superb for someone like me who can't sit still for long. Each day is just two or three pages and one breathing exercise, so I actually finished it. My sleep has improved a bit.
review.title: Small chapters, big difference

review.body: Cushioning is the best I've had in this budget, knees feel fine after long runs. The laces though are slippery and keep coming undone mid-run, I swapped them for an old pair. Still giving 5 because the shoe itself is great.
review.title: Love the cushioning, hate the laces

review.body: Phone heats up alot while charging and even on long video calls. Camera is ok in daylight but night shots come out grainy. Expected better at this price.
review.title: Heats up alot

review.body: Ordered UK 9 after checking the size chart and it fits exactly like my old pair. Toe box has a bit of room which I like for longer runs. Took a couple of days to break in.
review.title: True to size

review.body: Got this for my parents who are both in their late sixties and wanted to cut down on oily food. I was worried the buttons would confuse them but the touch panel with pictures of each food type is very clear, my father figured it out without calling me even once. The box was packed really well with thick foam on all sides, not a single scratch. Three weeks in and they've made aloo tikki, fish fry and even banana chips in it. Cleaning is just the basket and tray, both go straight into the sink.
review.title: Bought for my parents

review.body: Shadows over Hampi kept me up till 2 am. The boulder fields and temple ruins make a brilliant setting for a murder mystery, and the chapters are short so you keep saying just one more.
review.title: Perfect weekend read

review.body: Temperature knob is loose and doesn't match the actual heat. Put it on the cotton setting and it left a shiny burn mark on my husband's linen shirt. Using it very carefully now.
review.title: Burnt my linen shirt

review.body: Solid build and the locking collar feels safe even for overhead presses. Giving 2 stars only because the 20kg set arrived with 17.5kg worth of plates. Seller did replace it but took almost two weeks.
review.title: Good set, wrong plates shipped

review.body: Crispy fries with barely a spoon of oil. Love it.
Zero white cast on my dusky skin 🙌 Finally.
review.title: No white cast

review.body: For under 3k the sound is really good, clear vocals and decent bass. Case is small enough for the coin pocket of my jeans. If you don't want to spend a lot, go for it.
review.title: Value for money, go for it

review.body: Been using this for four months as my main phone. Gaming is smooth on medium settings, I play BGMI for an hour daily and it only gets slightly warm. The 5000 mAh battery easily lasts a day and a half with my usage, and the charger in the box is the fast one, no need to buy separately. Camera is decent in daylight, portrait mode edge detection is surprisingly good. Speaker is loud. At under 19k this is paisa vasool, recommended it to two friends already.
review.title: Paisa vasool phone

review.body: Recieved on time, works great. Using it every day.
The motor is powerful and grinding is quick. Only problem is the small chutney jar, the lid leaks from the sides when you run it at speed 3, so I have to hold it down with a cloth every time.
review.title: Chutney jar lid leaks

review.body: Recieved it in two days with a full-length cover. Swings fast and feels balanced, my clears reach the back line easily now. Grip is slightly thin for my hand so I added an overgrip.
review.title: Good racket for club level

review.body: Tension holds up and the metal clips feel strong. But the latex smell is very strong when new and the colours rubbed off on my hands the first few days.

Gifted it to my husband for our anniversary. The dial looks elegant and the watch keeps good time. The leather strap had a strong chemical smell for the first week, he kept it out on the balcony for two days before he could wear it.
review.title: Classy look, strap smell though

review.body: We grind idli and dosa batter twice a week and this 750W motor doesn't struggle at all, even with a full jar of soaked rice. I've also used the small jar for dry masalas like garam masala and coffee beans and it gives a fine powder in under a minute. The jars are heavy steel and the handles feel solid. Yes it's loud, but every mixer at this power level is loud, so I don't hold it against it. Six months of regular use and no issues with the motor or the coupler.
review.title: Handles idli batter and dry masala easily

review.body: The box was clearly dropped somewhere, the front panel came cracked. Had to raise a replacement which took 12 days. Can't say much about the purifier itself yet.
review.title: Arrived damaged

review.body: Read it in two sittings. The way the author moves between the grandmother's diary and the present day is beautifully done, and the ending stayed with me for days.
review.title: Couldn't put it down

review.body: Gifted it to my dad, he checks his steps every hour now 👍
The breathing exercises in the first month are genuinely useful. After that it just repeats the same advice with new anecdotes, could easily have been half the length.
Noticeably less frizz after drying, my hair actually looks smoother instead of puffy. The folding handle is handy for travel. Gets warm to hold after ten minutes but nothing serious.
review.title: Less frizz than my old dryer

review.body: It works as a basic bathroom speaker for podcasts. Sound is average, battery lasts a few days with light use. Wouldn't use it for music.
Fast, light, and the battery just keeps going.

The bands themselves are good quality, the tension is consistent and they haven't lost stretch in two months. The door anchor is the weak link, the foam strap started tearing within weeks and I'm scared it will slip and smack me in the face, so now I tie the band to my bed leg instead. Would have been 5 stars with a better anchor.
review.title: Bands good, door anchor not so much

review.body: Was working fine and then one morning it just cut off mid-use and smelled like burning plastic. Haven't dared to switch it on since. Waiting on the warranty claim now.
review.title: Stopped working after two months

review.body: Most formal shirts I've tried feel like plastic by afternoon in Chennai. This one is proper cotton, stays breathable through a full office day and doesn't crease too badly on the commute.
review.title: Breathable, finally

review.body: It is extremely loud, I'm sure the neighbours can hear it. Worse, the overload switch trips every time I grind urad dal for more than a minute, so I have to wait and restart it three or four times.
review.title: Overload trips constantly

review.body: Performance is better than I expected from an i5, I edit 1080p videos in DaVinci and exports are reasonable. The problem is noise. As soon as you push it the fan ramps up and it's loud enough that my wife asked if something was wrong with it. Bottom panel also gets quite warm on the lap. For normal browsing it's silent, so if you're not doing heavy work you won't notice. Keeping it, but heads up.
review.title: Quick machine but the fan gets loud

review.body: Hardware is good for the price, camera takes nice photos outdoors and 5G works fine in Pune. But it came with eleven preinstalled apps and the lock screen keeps showing ads. Took me an evening to disable everything.
review.title: Good hardware, too much bloatware

review.body: Charged it once when it arrived and I've trimmed every three days for almost a month on that single charge. Battery backup is excellent. Blades are sharp, no pulling, and the length dial clicks firmly into place.

Bought these for work from home. I'm on calls 5-6 hours a day and they don't press on my glasses at all. Mic picks up my voice clearly, colleagues stopped complaining about the pressure cooker in the background.
review.title: Comfortable for long work calls

review.body: Laptop itself boots and works, but the box was crushed and the lid has a crack near the hinge. It's been 12 days and the replacement request is still 'under review'. Not what you expect on a 55k purchase.
review.title: Arrived with a cracked corner

review.body: The writing deserves five stars. Every character, even the cranky munshi who only shows up in three chapters, feels like a real person, and the way the family's debts are revealed slowly through the ledger entries is clever. Taking off a star for the print though. The font is really small and the paper is thin enough that the next page shows through, which made reading at night a strain. Would happily buy a hardcover edition if they bring one out.
review.title: Lovely writing, tiny font

review.body: My hair fall had become really bad after shifting to Bangalore, clumps in the comb every morning. Started oiling twice a week with this, leaving it on for two hours before washing. After about a month the fall has reduced noticeably and my scalp feels less dry. Yes, the onion smell is there, but it goes away completely after one shampoo wash. For 349 rupees it is value for money, go for it if you can handle the smell for a few hours.
review.title: Hair fall reduced, smell is manageable

review.body: Sole started peeling off near the toe after just three weeks of evening runs. Really disappointed, these are not cheap.
review.title: Sole peeled in 3 weeks

review.body: worst phone ever, dont waste your money
Boils water in like 3 mins. Does the job.
Nice and light, recieved quickly too.

The story was actually pulling me in for the first hundred pages, so this rating is about the copy I received, not the writing. Pages 113 to 144 were printed twice and the chapters after that were simply missing, so I never found out how it ends. I raised a return request the same day and was told books are non-returnable once opened. Customer support kept sending the same copy-paste reply. Very frustrating experience for a 349 rupee book.
review.title: Misprinted copy, return refused

review.body: Dries hair in 10 min. Bit loud. Okay overall.
Strings came super loose out of the box and the grip tape started peeling within a week. For 2k I expected better finishing.
Lid doesnt lock properly after just one month, steam escapes from the side so the auto shut off takes forever to trigger. Not safe to leave it unattended now. Poor quality.
review.title: Lid broke in a month

review.body: I held off reviewing until I'd used it properly for a semester. Context: I'm a final year engineering student, so it's mostly VS Code, a few Docker containers, MATLAB, Chrome with way too many tabs, and Netflix at night. The i5 with 16 GB handles all of that without slowing down, and the SSD makes boot and app launches basically instant. Battery is the highlight for me. On a normal college day with Wi-Fi on and brightness around 60% I get 8 to 9 hours, so I've stopped carrying the charger. It's also light enough that I don't notice it in my bag. Keyboard has good travel and the backlight has two levels. The screen is sharp but only average outdoors, I'd call it 'fine' rather than great. Speakers are thin, use headphones. The webcam is grainy but fine for online viva calls. For what Kestrel is charging, I honestly don't think there's a better student laptop right now.
review.title: Three months in, a proper review

review.body: Every junior developer should read this once.
review.title: Must read for freshers

review.body: The fabric is gorgeous and very airy. But the maroon faded noticeably after the first wash even though I hand washed it, and now the collar looks a shade lighter than the body.
review.title: Lovely fabric, colour faded a bit

review.body: Room feels fresher and allergies are better 👍
Ok for the price. Nothing more, nothing less.
Started leaking from the bottom within a month.

Fit was perfect when it arrived, I tried it on and was happy. Washed it once in cold water on the gentle cycle exactly as the label says, and it came out noticeably shorter in the sleeves and tight across the chest. It now fits my 15 year old nephew better than me. The fabric also feels rougher after washing. The return window had closed by the time I washed it, so I'm stuck with it. If you buy, maybe size up, or better, wash it before the return period ends.
review.title: Shrank a full size after one wash

review.body: Arrived with a big dent near the base, packed in a thin polybag with no bubble wrap at all. Seller wanted an unboxing video before replacing it, which I obviously did not have. Bottle works but I paid for a new one, not a dented one.
review.title: Came dented, poor packing

review.body: Mostly things I had already picked up at work.
Less hair fall in 3 weeks. Superb oil.

I travel for work almost every week and these fit in a small pouch in my laptop bag. Five levels is enough for rows, presses and leg work. Full value for money, nothing else comes close at this price.
review.title: Perfect for hotel room workouts

review.body: Battery life is genuinely good, 7+ hours for me. Screen is the letdown, it's dim and colours look washed out next to my phone. Okay for office work, not for photo editing.

I grew up eating my paati's food and most cookbooks dumb these recipes down. This one doesn't. The Chettinad chapter has a proper pepper chicken that tastes the way I remember, and the Mangalorean section taught me to make neer dosa without it tearing every time. Every recipe has both cup and gram measurements, which helps a lot. The photographs are gorgeous and the hardcover feels sturdy enough to survive kitchen splashes. It looks lovely on the shelf too.
review.title: Finally a South Indian cookbook that gets it right

review.body: My skin does look brighter after a month and it absorbs quickly without any stickiness. But the smell is really strong, kind of metallic, and it lingers for a while. Using it only at night now.
review.title: Works, but that smell

review.body: Charging the case maybe once a week is all it needs, battery life is excellent. The fit is the issue, the left bud keeps slipping out when I run, even with the large tips. Fine for desk use.
review.title: Great battery, loose fit

review.body: Fits perfect and looks premium. Go for it!
Finally I can't hear my neighbour's drilling.

Honestly the content is very generic, mostly quotes and 'take a deep breath' type advice, but that's not even the main problem. The binding is just glue and by day six pages 40 to 70 had come loose and were falling out every time I opened it. The paper is so thin you can see the print from the other side. For a book that's supposed to calm you down, it mostly irritated me. Would not buy this edition again.
review.title: Pages fell out within a week

review.body: Moved up to the Smash Pro from an aluminium racket and the difference is huge. It's light enough that my wrist doesn't tire after an hour of doubles, and the slightly head-heavy balance gives my smashes real punch. Factory strings were around 22 lbs, I got it restrung at 26 at the local shop and now the control at the net is excellent. The full cover it comes with is decent too. For the price this is hard to beat for intermediate players.
review.title: Big upgrade from aluminium

review.body: Two weeks in and I have small whiteheads along my jawline that I never had before. Stopped using it and they are clearing up. Maybe it suits others, not me.
review.title: Broke me out

review.body: I cancelled my gym membership after the lockdown habits stuck and bought the IronGrip set instead. Switching from 5kg to 12.5kg takes maybe 20 seconds once you get used to the spin collars, and the plates sit snug with no clanking during rows. Knurling on the handle is grippy without tearing my palms. I've been doing shoulder press, goblet squats and curls three times a week for four months and nothing has loosened. If you are short on space and want progressive load at home, go for it.
review.title: Replaced my gym membership

review.body: Night mode really is quiet, quieter than my ceiling fan on speed one. My son used to wake up sneezing and that has mostly stopped since we started running it.
Living in Kochi I sweat the moment I step out. This stays matte for a good four or five hours and doesn't run into my eyes. No tanning on my arms after a beach trip either. Totally value for money.

Expected a lot more for 699. The chapters don't really build on each other, it reads like a collection of blog posts with a common cover. Half the JavaScript examples still use callback style code and an old build setup nobody uses anymore, so I spent more time fixing the snippets than learning from them. There is some decent advice on commit messages and code review near the end, but you can find the same thing free online.
review.title: Feels like stitched blog posts

review.body: Fast, light and folds into my bag. Love it.

Been using it daily for about two months now. Fries, paneer tikka, even reheating samosas, everything comes out crisp with maybe a teaspoon of oil. The basket coating has held up so far and it cleans easily with warm water. Preheat is quick. Only small gripe is the beep is loud and you can't turn it off, my kid wakes up if I use it late. The 4.2L size is enough for a family of four if you do two batches. Honestly one of the better kitchen purchases I've made.
review.title: Replaced half my deep frying

review.body: Bought this in November when the AQI outside was touching 400. Kept it running in a 150 sq ft bedroom with the door shut and the PM2.5 reading on its display dropped from around 280 to below 40 in about half an hour. Night mode is superb, the fan goes almost silent and the display light turns off completely, so it doesn't bother my sleep at all. My wife's morning cough has noticeably reduced. It's not cheap, but in this city it feels necessary rather than a luxury.
review.title: Superb for Delhi winters

review.body: Grip is excellent and it doesn't bunch up under my feet in warrior poses. Downside is the surface picks up every bit of dust and my cat's hair, and wiping it leaves it sticky for a while. Also smelled like a tyre shop for the first week.
review.title: Great grip, but a dust magnet

review.body: Learnt alot from the chapters on code review and error handling. Defintely recommend for anyone who has just started working in a team.

Two problems that made me regret this. First, with noise cancelling on there's a constant faint hiss when nothing is playing, very noticeable in a quiet room at night. Second, the microphone is useless outside, on a call from the street the other person heard more traffic than my voice. Indoors music sounds good, I'll give it that, but I bought ANC headphones for the ANC. Raised a complaint and support just sent me a reset guide I had already tried twice.
review.title: Hiss with ANC and poor mic outdoors

review.body: Good serum for the price. Dropper works well.

Took this Northbay jacket on a week-long Manali trip in October and it was easily the most used thing in my bag. The denim is thick and properly heavy, blocks the wind well, and layering a hoodie underneath still left room to move my arms. Stitching on the pockets and cuffs is neat with no loose threads, and after two washes there's no fading yet. It does feel a little stiff for the first few days but that's normal for good denim. Sizing matched the chart.
review.title: Survived a Manali trip

review.body: Used the Velocita helmet on three 40 km Sunday rides so far. The vents really do keep my head cooler than my old one and the dial at the back is easy to adjust even with gloves on. Looks a little bulky in photos but I care more about safety.
review.title: Cool head on long rides

review.body: Serum went from pale yellow to dark orange in under a month even though I kept the cap tight. Oxidised vitamin C is useless, and it left a faint orange tint on my fingers. Waste of money.
review.title: Turned orange within a month

review.body: Ice still there next morning 🧊 love it
Got the paperback for under 400 and honestly it's value for money, the writing is that good. Already lent it to my sister.

Sound is surprisingly loud and clear for something this small, took it to the beach and the waterproofing held up fine. But the Bluetooth keeps dropping if my phone is more than a couple of metres away.
review.title: Loud for its size

review.body: The narrow edge on the Groomwell blade makes shaping the cheek line much easier than my old trimmer. Washable head is a big plus, I just rinse it under the tap after every use.
review.title: Neat lines around the cheeks

review.body: The light blue colour bled in the very first wash and turned my white vest and a handkerchief bluish. Washed it separately the second time and the water was still blue. Fabric is fine otherwise but I can't trust it in a mixed load.
review.title: Dye ran in the first wash

review.body: Sturdy jars and very easy to clean.
Average earbuds. They do what they should.
It's a slow, literary family drama. Some parts held my attention, others didn't. Probably better suited to readers who like this genre than to me.

I mainly use it for green tea in the morning and the occasional cup noodles at night. The inside is stainless steel, which was the main reason I picked it over the all-plastic ones. The outer body does get quite hot while boiling, so it's not something you want kids touching. The power cord is around 70 cm, enough if your socket is right next to the counter. It's been about five months with no issues. For around 1,200 rupees it's pretty much what you'd expect, nothing more and nothing less.
review.title: Average kettle for the price

review.body: Colour lighter than the pics. Regular jacket otherwise.

I have combination skin that reacts to almost every vitamin C product I've tried, usually tiny bumps on the forehead within a week. This one has been fine for six weeks now. Texture is watery, sinks in within a minute, and there's no sticky film even in Chennai humidity. I keep it in the fridge since it comes in an amber bottle, and the colour has stayed light yellow so far. Price is fair for 30ml, one bottle lasts me about five weeks.
review.title: Finally a vitamin C that didn't break me out

review.body: The trim itself is clean and even, and the 0.5 mm steps on the guard let me keep a proper stubble length instead of guessing. It's light, fits the hand well and makes a soft hum rather than a buzz. My complaints: a full charge takes almost two hours, there's no quick charge, and the port is micro USB, so I need a separate cable when everything else I own is Type-C. The guard comb also has a little play in it when you press hard along the jawline. Still, for this price the results are good.
review.title: Great trim, slow charging

review.body: My physio asked me to do floor exercises at home and kneeling on the thinner mat I had was painful. This one has enough cushion that I can hold planks and bird-dogs without my knees complaining. Took a day to lie completely flat.
review.title: Good for knees

review.body: Guessed the killer by chapter four, the so called twist was obvious from a mile away. Dont understand the hype.
Grinds dosa batter really smooth, totally paisa vasool.
review.title: Paisa vasool mixer

review.body: Top button popped off the second time I wore it, the metal shank just snapped. Raised a return and the pickup got cancelled twice without anyone calling me. Still didnt get my refund after 10 days.
review.title: Button gone, return a mess

review.body: They're fine. Sound is clear, ANC is average, nothing like the premium brands but you're paying a third of the price. Using them mostly at the gym.

First time I used it there was a burning smell from the motor and I almost packed it up for return. Checked the manual and it actually says a slight smell is normal for new motors, so I gave it a few more tries with short bursts. By the third use it was completely gone. That was four months ago and it's been running fine since, we use it daily for chutneys and the big jar for buttermilk on weekends. Taking one star off only because the manual should have said this in bold on the first page.
review.title: Burning smell went away after a few runs

review.body: The green band snapped near the clip on my fifth squat of the day and whipped my forearm, left a red welt for two days. Had been using it barely three weeks. Won't trust the others now.
review.title: Snapped and hit my arm

review.body: Threads got stripped within a month. Dont buy.
The recipes and photos are wonderful, no complaints there. But it came in a thin plastic cover with no box and the corner of the hardcover was badly dented. Giving 2 stars for that.
review.title: Love the book, hate the condition

review.body: TDS went from 650 to about 90 according to the technician's meter. Taste is fine. It takes more wall space than the old one and the storage tank is around 7 litres, which is enough for two people.
Seeing a lot of complaints about pairing, but mine has been fine with an iPhone for two months. Strap is handy for hanging it on the shower rod and the bass is decent.
Charges from 10 to 80 in half an hour. Love it.
Been using 3-4 drops every morning before sunscreen. The dark spots near my cheeks have faded a bit and overall my skin looks fresher. Absorbs fast and doesn't pill under makeup.
Light texture and it blends in quickly. I use it every morning before work and haven't had any breakouts so far. Would like a bigger tube though.
It's a plain white shirt and it does what a plain white shirt does. Slim fit is genuinely slim, so size up if you have broad shoulders.

My mother uses it for the online classes she teaches and for video calls with family abroad. Setup took ten minutes and she figured out the fingerprint login herself. Webcam is clear enough, she's happy and so am I.
review.title: Bought for my mother

review.body: It's fine for slow yoga and stretching. For HIIT and jumping workouts it feels thinner than 6mm and I can feel the floor. Colour is as shown.

The carton was torn open on one side when it arrived and the plates were just loose inside with no wrapping. Three of the plates already had brown rust spots and one handle had a dent in the knurling. I raised a return the same evening, the pickup was cancelled twice without any call and support kept sending the same copy-paste reply. Got my refund after 18 days. Maybe I got a bad unit but the whole experience was frustrating.
review.title: Rust spots out of the box

review.body: Got these in the festive sale for my husband. He uses them for gym and evening walks, says they're comfortable and the grey colour looks smart with jeans too.
Zero slipping, even in a 40 minute hot flow.
Slow start, but a very rewarding read.
review.title: Worth the hype

review.body: I had a 25L OTG before this and honestly the Crispo is better for everyday stuff. It heats up in about two minutes instead of ten, the digital panel shows time and temperature together, and the shake reminder halfway is a nice touch. Chicken wings come out crisp outside and juicy inside. The OTG still wins for baking a full cake, but for snacks, roasted veggies and frozen stuff this has replaced it completely. Footprint on the counter is smaller than I expected too.
review.title: Switched from an OTG, no regrets

review.body: Dropper leaks a little, the bottle is tiny and the smell is not pleasant. Still, my skin tone looks more even than before, so I'll probably buy it again.
review.title: Lots of small issues but it works

review.body: There are three heat settings and two speeds on paper, but in practice the low setting is almost as hot as high. With thin, colour-treated hair that's a problem, the ends started feeling dry and straw-like within a couple of weeks. The cool shot button only works if you keep it pressed the whole time, which gets tiring. It's also much louder than I expected, my neighbour joked that I was running a mixer at 7 am. Drying speed is decent, I'll give it that, but I've gone back to air drying most days.
review.title: Heat settings are misleading

review.body: Its okay. Dries matte, a bit drying on cheeks.

I do power yoga five mornings a week and my old mat used to turn into a slip-n-slide by the second round of sun salutations. This one actually grips better as my palms get sweaty, which I did not expect. The 6mm thickness is a big relief for my knees in low lunges and cat-cow. There was a rubbery smell for the first two or three days, I left it unrolled on the balcony and it went away. No peeling or marks after about two months of daily use.
review.title: Grip holds up even in sweaty sessions

review.body: Food cooks evenly and the presets for fries and chicken are pretty accurate. But after three months the non-stick in the basket has started scratching even though I only use the silicone tongs that came with it.
review.title: Basket coating needs care
